cards.front: What is the difference between registration and title, what ages apply, and how soon must new residents register?
cards.back: Registration permits road use while the title proves ownership; registration needs age sixteen, titling any age, and new residents must register within thirty days.

cards.front: How do registration and title differ in purpose and in deadlines for new residents?
cards.back: Registration grants road permission while the title proves ownership, and new residents face a thirty-day registration clock with no matching title deadline.

cards.front: What do you need to register a vehicle, and what do you receive?
cards.back: Registering demands ownership or owner authorization, insurance, paid sales taxes, and odometer and damage statements on form MV-eighty-two with six-point name and birth-date proof, per guide MV-eighty-two point one, yielding plates, a document and a sticker; non-dealer buys add a ten-day inspection extension on request, while dealer cars must carry an inspection from within thirty days.

cards.front: What may a registered dealer do for a buyer at registration time?
cards.back: Registered dealers may register the car for the buyer with temporary paperwork and plates for a processing fee plus state fees.

cards.front: How many insurance identification cards does an insurer issue, and what must match on them?
cards.back: Insurers issue two identification cards whose names and VIN must match the application exactly, one presented at registration and one kept in the car.

decks.module: Proof of ownership and title checks

cards.front: What ownership papers go with each kind of vehicle purchase?
cards.back: Dealer-new ownership is a manufacturer origin certificate plus MV-fifty sale certificate, dealer-used is the prior MV-nine hundred ninety-nine title with odometer and salvage statements plus MV-fifty, non-registering dealers must still hand over those papers with a signed MV-eighty-two, out-of-state-dealer used cars need signed-over title or transferable registration with bill and proofs, and private-used needs the signed-over MV-nine hundred ninety-nine or a transferable registration for nineteen-seventy-two and older with signed odometer and damage acknowledgments.

cards.front: How does dealer sale paperwork differ from private sale paperwork?
cards.back: Dealer sales pair origin or title papers with MV-fifty while private sales lean on the signed-over title alone, and only dealer paperwork can skip the buyer's own MV-eighty-two trip.

cards.front: What should a buyer check on a title before accepting it, and why?
cards.back: Before accepting any title, buyers check its face for lien holders showing unpaid vehicle loans, demand a lender release, or risk repossession by the lien holder.

cards.front: Which titles will a motor vehicle office reject?
cards.back: Offices reject titles lacking completed odometer or damage statements or showing alterations, erasures or cancellations, even of a name or signature.

cards.front: Which vehicles need odometer and damage statements, and what must the buyer do?
cards.back: Cars eight model years old or newer need both seller-completed and buyer-signed odometer and damage statements that may brand the new title Rebuilt Salvage; cars ten model years or newer need the odometer statement on the title back while damage disclosure drops off at nine model years and older, and buyers initial the odometer box and match it to the dash reading.

cards.front: At what model-year age do the damage and odometer disclosure rules stop?
cards.back: Damage disclosure dies at nine model years while odometer disclosure survives to ten, an off-by-one pair that traps skimmers.

cards.front: What must happen before a Rebuilt Salvage vehicle is registered or titled?
cards.back: Rebuilt Salvage or similar-worded vehicles must pass a stolen-parts examination before registration or titling, and out-of-state titled buys warrant a call-center check first.

cards.front: Who collects sales tax when you buy a vehicle, and when is the private-sale tax form needed?
cards.back: Registered dealers collect sales tax directly, while other sellers trigger form DTF-eight hundred two with buyer-completed price certification and a seller signature when the price trails market value or the car is a non-family gift, defaulting otherwise to market-value tax at registration.

cards.front: How is sales tax handled for a dealer purchase compared with a private purchase?
cards.back: Dealer purchases bake sales tax into the deal while private buys file DTF-eight hundred two, and missing seller signatures default the tax to market value rather than the claimed price.

cards.front: How long do most registrations run, and how do plate refunds work?
cards.back: Most registrations to eighteen thousand pounds run two years on weight-based fees plus plate and title fees, used plates kill any refund, unused plates returned within sixty days refund fully minus processing, second-year fees refund when only the first year was used, plate turn-ins need receipt FS-6T, and transfer credit follows only the replacement vehicle.

cards.front: What should you remove before selling or trading a vehicle, and why?
cards.back: Sellers and traders strip plates and the windshield sticker first, or strangers parking tickets may bill the old owner.

cards.front: How often do registrations renew, and when might you not get a reminder?
cards.back: Renewals run every two years with mailed reminders forty-five to sixty days out, lost when addresses lapse, three-plus parking tickets stand unanswered, or credentials are suspended, plus two weeks of processing that the owner must anticipate without excuse.

cards.front: What happens when a registration expires on a weekend or state holiday?
cards.back: Expiries landing on weekends or state holidays stretch automatically to midnight of the next business day with insurance maintained throughout.

cards.front: How do you renew a registration by mail?
cards.back: Mail renewal files MV-eighty-two with a separate note for alternate mailing, since addresses written on MV-eighty-two join the record while MV-two hundred thirty-two alone changes every record, plus a check to the Commissioner with MV-204A fee lookup and an insurance card when carriers changed, sent to the Utica processing center with two weeks of patience, longer overseas, and name changes demand an office visit with identity proofs.

cards.front: Who may renew a registration online, and how does it work?
cards.back: Online renewal fits unchanged addresses and carriers on passenger cars, small trucks and non-exclusive-off-road motorcycles, showing fees on screen for three-step credit-card renewal mailed within two weeks.

cards.front: What is needed to renew a registration in person, including through someone else?
cards.back: In-person renewal files MV-eighty-two with the registrant's signature, and second parties including spouses must show original identification for themselves plus original or copy for the registrant.

cards.front: How do the mail, online and office renewal paths differ?
cards.back: Mail renewal tolerates address changes with a side note, online renewal forbids any address or carrier change, and office visits demand the registrant's own signature even through a proxy.

cards.front: When must a registered vehicle be insured?
cards.back: A registered vehicle must stay liability-insured whether driven or parked.

cards.front: What are the minimum liability insurance amounts?
cards.back: Minimum coverage is fifty thousand for one death and one hundred thousand for two or more, twenty-five thousand for one injury and fifty thousand for two or more, and ten thousand for property, all per incident.

cards.front: How do the death and injury minimums compare at each headcount?
cards.back: Death minimums run fifty and one hundred thousand while injury runs twenty-five and fifty with ten for property, so death always doubles injury at each headcount.

cards.front: What must you do before your insurance coverage lapses?
cards.back: Before coverage lapses, plates go back with an FS-6T receipt or daily civil penalties or registration suspension follow, ninety uninsured days without returned plates suspend the license too, DMV insurance letters demand answers, and motorcycles skip the plate turn-in.

cards.front: How are motorcycles treated differently when insurance lapses?
cards.back: Motorcycles must carry insurance like cars yet skip the plate turn-in on lapse, the chapter's cleanest exception to a universal rule.

cards.front: Who must prove insurance to drive in the state, and what is the penalty for uninsured driving?
cards.back: Everyone driving or lending a car in the state, resident or not, must prove acceptable insurance, and uninsured driving, lending or crashing revokes at least one year.

cards.front: How soon must a vehicle be inspected after a purchase?
cards.back: In-state-sold vehicles need inspection within thirty days with a certificate before delivery, non-dealer buys need it within ten days of registration with a VS-one thousand seventy-seven extension on request, and a mover's existing certificate survives to expiry or one year, whichever first.

cards.front: What are the three inspection clocks for dealer buyers, private buyers and movers?
cards.back: Dealer-bought cars enjoy thirty inspection days while private buys get ten after registration, and movers keep an old certificate up to a year, three clocks for three buyer kinds.

cards.front: Which retail transfers are exempt from inspection?
cards.back: Retail inspection exemptions cover welfare-to-work transfers, chassis transfers, factory-direct delivery, out-of-state or country registration, scrap, and lease buyouts.

cards.front: When is re-inspection due, and where are vehicles inspected?
cards.back: Re-inspection falls due before the current certificate expires and on every registrant change, at yellow-and-black official stations, with heavy trucks, buses, tractors and trailers at heavy-vehicle stations and motorcycles at motorcycle stations.

cards.front: What does signing a renewal certify, and what happens after an inspection?
cards.back: Signing a renewal certifies the inspection is current, owners track the annual date and book early for repair time, passers earn a windshield sticker while failures get a rejection notice demanding repair and retest.

cards.front: When can a failed emissions inspection be waived, and which vehicles take safety only?
cards.back: Failed high-enhanced or OBD II emissions inspections can waive after a genuine repair attempt costing at least four hundred fifty dollars; most gasoline cars take emissions with safety except motorcycles, and cars twenty-six-plus or under-two model years old plus historic registrations take safety only.

cards.front: What inspections apply to diesel vehicles?
cards.back: Diesels running in the state face random roadside safety checks even when registered elsewhere, and ratings over eighty-five hundred pounds add a diesel emissions inspection.

cards.front: What should a buyer do about a problem with a dealer, station or repair shop?
cards.back: The DMV licenses dealers, stations and repair shops, so buyers verify credentials, complain to management first, then call weekdays eight-thirty to four-fifteen or write the Albany consumer box, with repair complaints due within ninety days or three thousand miles, whichever first.

recap_hooks.text: Registration lets you drive on the road; the title proves you own the car, and new residents register within thirty days.
Register with ownership proof, insurance, paid sales tax and form MV-eighty-two, and keep one insurance card in the car.

recaps.module: Proof of ownership and title checks

recap_hooks.text: Check every title for liens and missing statements before accepting it.
Damage disclosure ends at nine model years, odometer disclosure at ten.
Dealers collect sales tax; private buyers file form DTF-eight hundred two.
Take your plates and windshield sticker off before you sell.
Renew every two years; mail allows a side note, online needs no changes, and office visits need the registrant's signature.
Fifty and one hundred thousand for death, twenty-five and fifty for injury, ten for property.
Return plates before coverage lapses, except motorcycles.
Dealer buys inspect within thirty days, private buys within ten after registration, and movers keep a valid certificate up to a year.
